name: PixiTween Director S15c: catalog studio (wall, live player, capture, price edit, product page, Publish)
description: The browser side of Catalog Crew: import a feed on a finished film, watch the catalog wall fill with one live player and one hidden capture player, edit a price and see it update, open a product page mock, and optionally publish MP4s through Clippy's renderer into a feed CSV. Everything except Publish plays live in the browser.

userStories.title: Catalog API client and useCatalog hook
userStories.description: As a catalog page, I want one hook that loads a catalog and applies catalog events live so that every component shows the same state.
steps: Read web/src/api/client.ts (request, api), web/src/api/sse.ts (useFilmEvents) and shared/catalog.ts.
Edit web/src/api/client.ts: add api.createCatalog(form), api.getCatalog(id), api.getFilmCatalog(filmId) and api.patchProduct(catalogId, productId, patch).

Create web/src/catalog/catalogReducer.ts: a pure reducer applying catalog.created, catalog.variant and catalog.product events to a Catalog, ignoring events for other catalog ids and variant updates older than the stored version.

Create web/src/catalog/useCatalog.ts: useCatalog(catalogId) fetches the catalog, subscribes to the master film's events with useFilmEvents, and returns { catalog, loading, error, counts: { ready, flagged, building, failed } }.
Add web/src/catalog/catalogReducer.test.ts and web/src/catalog/useCatalog.test.tsx with a mocked fetch and a fake event list.
acceptanceCriteria: Applying catalog.variant { status: 'ready', version: 3 } then { status: 'checking', version: 2 } leaves status 'ready'
useCatalog('cat_x') requests /api/catalogs/cat_x once and counts.ready equals the number of ready variants after events arrive
An event for another catalog id leaves the state unchanged
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: Hidden capture player answers price-check frame requests
userStories.description: As a price check, I want the catalog page to photograph each product's film on request so that the crew can read the price it shows.
steps: Read web/src/crew/useCaptureRequests.ts (answerCapture, CAPTURE_MAX_AGE_MS), web/src/capture/driver.ts and the capture.request event (optional filmId from S15b).
Edit web/src/crew/useCaptureRequests.ts: export a CaptureRequest filmId field read from the event, and let answerCapture post to req.filmId when set (default: the stream's film).

Create web/src/catalog/CaptureLane.tsx: keeps a FIFO of capture requests that carry a filmId, loads one film at a time into a single hidden Player (off-screen, same size as the composition, preserveDrawingBuffer on), waits for it, calls answerCapture, then moves to the next.
Skip requests older than CAPTURE_MAX_AGE_MS; show a small 'Checking N' counter in the page header.
Mount CaptureLane once in CatalogPage.
Add web/src/catalog/CaptureLane.test.tsx with fake capture deps.
acceptanceCriteria: Three requests for films f1, f2, f3 are answered in order, each posted to its own film id
At no time are two hidden Players mounted (the test counts mounted Players)

Edit server/env.ts and .env.example: CLIPPY_RENDER_TOOL (default 'render_composition'), CLIPPY_RENDER_STATUS_TOOL (default 'get_render_status'), CATALOG_PUBLISH boolOff.

Edit server/clippy/types.ts: renderArgsSchema { composition (object), width, height, fps, format: 'mp4' }, renderSubmitSchema { jobId, status }, renderStatusSchema { status: 'queued' | 'rendering' | 'done' | 'failed', url?, error?, credits? }.

userStories.title: Publish service, routes and the feed CSV

Create server/http/handlers/catalog-publish.ts: POST /api/catalogs/:id/publish (passcode; 409 when CATALOG_PUBLISH is false; 202 and runs in the background) and GET /api/catalogs/:id/feed.csv (text/csv attachment). Edit server/http/routes.ts to register them.

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.
For engine behaviour (composition JSON, Player, timeline, layer kinds) read docs/engine/README.md before writing code; never edit or copy engine source.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.
At most two engine Players are mounted on any catalog page: the visible one and the hidden capture one. Browsers cap live WebGL canvases (about 16 in Chrome); a grid of live players is not allowed.
Wall tiles show the product's cut-out or photo as a still image, never a live player.
Publish is optional and off by default (CATALOG_PUBLISH=false). The catalog page works fully without Clippy.
The Clippy render tool name comes from CLIPPY_RENDER_TOOL; never hard-code a guess elsewhere. The owner confirms the real name in MG-1.

ui: Verify in the browser (dev-browser skill or preview): `npm run dev`, open the page named in the story, confirm the stated behaviour, and record what you saw in `notes`

manualGates: MG-1: owner confirms the Clippy render tool's name, arguments and result shape (composition JSON in, MP4 URL out), whether it renders model3d layers and the MSDF fonts, and sets CLIPPY_RENDER_TOOL.
MG-2: owner publishes 3 products of a live catalog through Clippy and compares one Clippy frame with the browser frame at the same time; records seconds and credits per product.
MG-3: owner checks the catalog page in Chrome with 30 products: no lost WebGL context in the console after selecting 10 products in a row.
